about: A server that streams video from torrents while they download, so a TV or player can start watching right away.

prs.title: Local network IPv6 clients are not banned
prs.broken: With any IP list set, devices on the local network over IPv6 were banned by mistake.
prs.changed: The server now reads their address correctly.
prs.matters: Home network devices keep working when an IP list is on.

prs.title: Blocked-site rules work for non-English domains
prs.broken: A blocked-site rule for a domain in Cyrillic or another script never matched what browsers send.
prs.changed: Rules now match both forms of such domains.
prs.matters: Blocking works for every domain, not just English ones.

prs.title: Empty settings requests are refused cleanly
prs.broken: Saving settings without any settings crashed the request with an empty error.
prs.changed: The server now answers with a clear bad-request message.
prs.matters: Apps see what went wrong instead of a crash.

prs.title: A bad torrent ID gets a clear answer
prs.broken: A torrent ID in the wrong shape crashed the request and returned an empty error.
prs.changed: Those requests now get a plain not found.
prs.matters: Apps get a clear answer and the log stays clean.

prs.title: Playlists refresh when they change
prs.broken: The playlist's version tag came only from the torrent and file name. After a file was marked watched, the list changed but the tag did not, so players kept the old list.
prs.changed: The tag now comes from the playlist's own content, so it changes whenever the list does.
prs.matters: Players always get the current playlist, including the resume-from-last-watched list.

prs.title: Two torrents with the same title can both be opened
prs.broken: In the network drive and mounted folder views, two torrents with the same title showed up as two folders with one name, and opening either always opened the first one. The second torrent could not be reached.
prs.changed: When titles clash, each folder gets a short piece of its torrent's ID added to its name. Unique titles stay as they are.
prs.matters: Every torrent in a category can be browsed and played, even when titles repeat.

prs.title: Episode 1 no longer shows episode 10's subtitles
prs.broken: A subtitle was matched to a video when its name started with the video's name. So episode 1 also picked up the subtitles for episodes 10 and 11, and choosing one played the wrong episode's text.
prs.changed: The matching name now has to end at a word break, so Show - 1 no longer matches Show - 10.
prs.matters: Each episode lists only its own subtitles.

prs.title: Episodes stop pulling in other episodes as extra tracks
prs.broken: The playlist attached every file whose name contained the video's name as an extra audio or subtitle track. In a season pack, episode 1 got episodes 10 and 11 and episode 10's audio attached to it in VLC.
prs.changed: An extra file now has to carry the whole video name, followed by something that is not a letter or digit.
prs.matters: VLC loads only the tracks that belong to the episode being played.

prs.title: Ukrainian and other Cyrillic subtitles now show every letter
prs.broken: Subtitles saved in an old Windows Cyrillic format only had Russian letters mapped. Ukrainian, Belarusian and Serbian letters, and signs like the copyright mark, came out as question boxes.
prs.changed: The converter now knows every character in that format, in both directions.
prs.matters: Viewers watching with Ukrainian or other Cyrillic subtitles can read every line, and the original file can be downloaded unchanged.

prs.title: Titles with a percent sign are no longer lost
prs.broken: When a torrent was added with a title like 100 percent Pure Show written with the percent sign, the server decoded it twice, failed, and saved no title at all. Posters, categories and searches had the same problem.
prs.changed: The server still tries the second decode, but keeps the text as it arrived when that fails.
prs.matters: Torrents keep the names people give them, and searches with a percent sign still work.

prs.title: Episode 1 now comes before Episode 10
prs.broken: Files with unpadded episode numbers were listed out of order: Episode 10, 11 and 12 came before Episode 1. Playlists followed that order, so a player started at episode 10.
prs.changed: The sort now compares the whole episode number, so 1 is weighed against 10 as a number.
prs.matters: A season plays from the first episode in the right order.

prs.title: The combined playlist plays the episode it names
prs.broken: With the option to merge all playlists into one turned on, entries could play a different file than their name said. The combined list and the stream used two different sort orders.
prs.changed: The combined list now sorts files the same way the stream does before numbering them.
prs.matters: Picking an episode from the combined playlist plays that episode.

prs.title: Resetting settings turns the network services back on
prs.broken: Resetting settings to defaults stopped media sharing, network discovery and the search service and started none of them. The defaults said discovery was on, but the server was not visible until a restart.
prs.changed: A reset now restarts each service that the new settings turn on, the same way saving settings does.
prs.matters: After a reset the server shows up on the network without a restart.
